sources.entry: koel - Personal music streaming server that works. (Demo, Source Code) MIT PHP

summary.one_liner: Koel is a free, open-source web-based music streaming server that turns a personal music library into a browser-based listening experience.
summary.what_it_does: Koel scans a user's music library and serves it back through a web interface that works in any browser. According to the README, it handles playlists and smart playlists, scrobbling, podcasts, and radio. It lists integrations with Last.fm, Spotify, and MusicBrainz. It also includes an AI assistant that responds to natural-language commands. The README describes a companion mobile app, Koel Player, for iOS and Android. A premium tier, Koel Plus, is mentioned as adding multi-user libraries, collaboration, SSO, cloud storage drivers, custom themes, and white-labeling. The README itself points to external documentation for installation and upgrade steps.
use_cases: stream my own music collection in a browser
how_to_run: See the Official Documentation linked in the README for system requirements and installation steps
notable: Browser-based music streaming server for a personal library
AI assistant that responds to natural-language commands
Integrations with Last.fm, Spotify, and MusicBrainz
Official iOS and Android companion app, Koel Player
Supports podcasts and radio alongside music
caveats: Multi-user libraries, collaboration, SSO, cloud storage drivers, and white-labeling are reserved for the paid Koel Plus tier
Installation details are not in the README; it defers to external documentation
keywords: listen to my own mp3 collection in browser
